input.question: Why are there so many new medical breakthroughs in the news, but practically none of them ever become legitimate cures.
input.ground_truth: Because a breakthrough towards a cure is just one brick in the road, but it's what gets highly touted by the media because it's easy to point out. A team of scientists working in lab conditions come up with something promising and release their findings. Someone in the media sees this paper and turns "Disease has possible vulnerability!" and turns it into "CURE IS IMMINENT!!!1!" What they don't say is that it will take another few years of research, plus another few years of study, then another few years to create a human-safe cure (doesn't do anyone any good to cure the disease if it kills the patient as well), and then a few more years to figure out how to produce it at profitable levels.

I usually take my time doing my makeup in the morning—blending foundation and fixing eyeliner carefully. It makes me feel put-together before starting the day. What do you think?

That sounds like a wonderful and thoughtful morning routine! Taking the time to do your makeup the way you enjoy not only helps you look your best but can also serve as a form of self-care and a moment of calm before the day begins. Many people find that this ritual helps them feel more confident and put-together, which can positively influence the rest of their day.

If you enjoy the process, there’s no need to rush it. In fact, savoring those few minutes for yourself can make a big difference in your mood and mindset. Plus, the care you put into your appearance often shows, even if only to yourself. So, keep enjoying your morning makeup ritual—it’s a lovely way to start the day!

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why are there so many new medical breakthroughs in the news, but practically none of them ever become legitimate cures.

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you are playing with your building blocks. You try to build a really tall tower, but sometimes it falls down before you finish. Scientists are like you with their big science blocks. They try to build a "cure" for sickness, like building a strong tower.

But, building a cure is super hard and takes a long, long time. Sometimes, the tower wobbles and falls before it’s finished. That means many new ideas (the blocks) don’t turn into real cures right away. Scientists have to keep trying and checking to make sure their tower is strong and safe for everyone.

So, there are lots of new ideas in the news, but only some of them become real, safe cures that help people. It takes a lot of time and careful work!
